pharm: Sulfonamide-derived inhibitor of carbonic anhydrase II that reduces aqueous humor formation in the ciliary body to lower intraocular pressure.
quick: 1 drop in affected eye(s) 3 times daily; shake well
No human data; use only if benefit outweighs risk
IOP; corneal endothelium (low cell counts); signs of sulfa reaction
summary: Brinzolamide 1% ophthalmic suspension is a topical carbonic anhydrase inhibitor used to lower elevated intraocular pressure in ocular hypertension or open-angle glaucoma. The usual dose is one drop in the affected eye(s) three times daily after shaking the bottle. Although applied to the eye, it is a sulfonamide that is absorbed systemically, so sulfa-type hypersensitivity reactions can occur. Most common side effects are blurred vision and a bitter or unusual taste.
indications: Elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) in patients with ocular hypertension
Elevated IOP in patients with open-angle glaucoma

dosage.c: Elevated IOP (ocular hypertension or open-angle glaucoma)
dosage.t: Three times daily in the affected eye(s)

dosage.n: Separate different ophthalmic drops by at least 10 minutes

admin: Shake the bottle well before each use (suspension)
Instill one drop into the affected eye(s) three times daily
Do not let the dropper tip touch the eye or any surface to avoid contamination
If using more than one topical ophthalmic drug, space doses at least 10 minutes apart
Remove soft contact lenses before instillation; reinsert 15 minutes later (contains benzalkonium chloride)
moa: Inhibits carbonic anhydrase II in the ciliary processes of the eye, slowing bicarbonate ion formation and the subsequent sodium and fluid transport that drive aqueous humor secretion; reduced aqueous formation lowers intraocular pressure.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to brinzolamide or any component of the product
relative: Low corneal endothelial cell counts (risk of corneal edema)
Acute angle-closure glaucoma (not studied; needs additional therapy)
monitor: Corneal status in low endothelial cell counts

preg: No adequate well-controlled human studies; oral dosing in rats produced fetal toxicity at ~375 times the recommended human ophthalmic dose. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: It is not known whether topically applied brinzolamide is excreted in human milk; exercise caution when administering to a breastfeeding woman.
renal: Not studied in severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min); because brinzolamide and its metabolite are excreted predominantly by the kidney, use is not recommended in such patients.
hepatic: Use in hepatic impairment has not been specifically studied; use with caution.

major: Oral carbonic anhydrase inhibitors (e.g., acetazolamide) - additive systemic carbonic anhydrase inhibition; concomitant use not recommended
moderate: High-dose salicylate therapy - potential acid-base and electrolyte alterations
interactions.diagnostics: Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors can cause acid-base/electrolyte changes with high-dose salicylates; monitor potassium and pH if overdose suspected.

serious: Corneal edema in patients with low endothelial cell counts

monitoring: Corneal status, especially in patients with low endothelial cell counts
Signs/symptoms of serious sulfonamide hypersensitivity (rash, blistering, blood dyscrasia)
Renal function consideration before use (avoid if CrCl <30 mL/min)
counsel: Shake the bottle well before each use
Vision may be temporarily blurred after instillation; use care driving or operating machinery
Do not touch the dropper tip to the eye or any surface to prevent contamination
Stop the drops and seek medical advice immediately if you develop a rash, blistering, or other signs of an allergic/sulfa reaction
Remove soft contact lenses before use and reinsert 15 minutes afterward
If using other eye drops, wait at least 10 minutes between products
pk: Reduces IOP after topical ocular dosing
Plasma levels low/below assay limits; RBC carbonic anhydrase II saturated within ~4 weeks
Very long in whole blood (~111 days) due to RBC carbonic anhydrase binding
Store at 4 C to 30 C (39 F to 86 F); shake well; use until expiration after opening
pearls: Despite topical use, brinzolamide is a sulfonamide that is absorbed systemically - same hypersensitivity reactions as oral sulfonamides can occur
Distributes extensively into red blood cells via carbonic anhydrase II binding, giving an exceptionally long whole-blood half-life (~111 days)
Do not combine with an oral carbonic anhydrase inhibitor (additive systemic effects)
IOP-lowering efficacy was not demonstrated in pediatric patients 4 weeks to 5 years old (dosed twice daily in trials)
Benzalkonium chloride preservative can be absorbed by soft contact lenses
missed: Apply the missed dose as soon as remembered; if it is near the next scheduled dose, skip it and resume the regular three-times-daily schedule. Do not instill extra drops to make up for a missed dose.
overdose: No human overdose data. Systemic (oral) overdose may cause electrolyte imbalance, an acidotic state, and possible CNS effects; monitor serum electrolytes (particularly potassium) and blood pH and provide supportive care.
